text:
Samir: FYI, on the Node onboarding sampleapp I just noticed debug logs leaking partial API token fragments when the SDK log level is set to debug. not full key but still 😬
Lina: ugh. which SDK version?
Samir: node-sdk v0.9.4. Go sampleapp (go-sdk v0.6.1) doesn't show the fragments. might be a stringify + header log path difference.
Priya: can you paste a redacted example? helps reproduce quickly.
Samir: sure — here's the console output (redacted):
```
DEBUG 2026-03-23T20:12:02Z http.request headers={"content-type":"application/json","authorization":"Bearer sk-REDACT_ME_abc123"} body={"prompt":"hello"}
```
Samir: the Node SDK's http-logger serializes headers before redaction runs. in Go we redact header values at the http transport level so it never prints.
Evan: does this affect only Authorization or nested json too?
Samir: nested. our onboarding sample event pings include a field `user.identities[0].token` in some customers' telemetry and that isn't caught by the current header-only redactor.
Lina: oh — our redaction rules are currently configured as key-name matches at top-level headers + top-level body keys. the config is: `redact_keys: ["authorization","api_key","password"]` — no deep-path support.
Priya: that's probably the main gap. two fixes: 1) move redaction earlier in Node SDK request pipeline (before logger.serialize). 2) extend redaction matcher to support JSONPath-ish deep-key matching.
Samir: agree. also spotted an OTEL propagation gap: traces have traceparent but the `request_id` attribute we inject in the go runtime via middleware isn't being attached by node. so spans are missing request_id attribute so trace->log correlation breaks.
Evan: are we using the same hook order across sdks? Node has `initOtel()` called after logger setup in the sampleapp, Go does it before. order matters because our logger attaches a log hook to read active span attributes; if OTEL init happens after, logs miss span attrs.
Lina: reproducible steps?
Samir: repo: `samples/onboard-node` branch `telemetry-fix` — run `LOG_LEVEL=debug node app.js` and hit /generate. check console for `request_id` key in logs.
Priya: can we add a unit/integration test to CI that ensures:
- With LOG_LEVEL=debug the SDK never outputs anything matching `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]`
- Logs include `request_id` when otel is initialized
Lina: yeah. I'll add a smoke test using the sampleapp harness. also propose: normalize log-level mapping across sdks. Node has custom levels (`silly, verbose, info, warn, error`) and our runtime uses `debug, info, warn, error`. mapping mismatch means in some environments debug logs are suppressed.
Evan: mapping bug hit me today — ops couldn't see our KV cache warm logs because Node treated them as `verbose` and our infra `LOG_LEVEL=debug` didn't enable verbose.
Samir: suggested fix: expose a canonical enum `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL` and map sdk-specific levels to it. update docs and sampleapps.
dev-telemetry-bot: Created issue <https://issues.redwood.ai/4521|#4521> "sampleapp: deep-redaction + otel propagation parity across SDKs" and queued a smoke test. :white_check_mark:
Priya: I'll pick up the deep-redaction matcher and a patch to run redaction pre-serialize in Node. aiming for PR by EOD tomorrow.
Lina: I'll do the log-level mapping RFC and add the smoke test in CI.
Evan: I'll update onboarding docs to call `initOtel()` earlier in the Node sample and add a note about level mapping.
Samir: thanks team. leaving a minimal patch in my branch that demonstrates redaction ordering. ping me if you want to pair. :eyes:
Priya: +1, will pair for node transport hooks later today.
Samir: marking as resolved locally but keeping thread open until PRs merged. :party-parrot:
